case_evidence.description: Frozen Python shared-multiplier FPCR inference truncation scan over unique consecutive candidates h >= fixed residual/pseudo-truth k with complete trajectories, target configuration and scientific NumPy RNG settings; explicit source-mode canonical output.

Complete 24-curve observed-grid source FPCA, k=2, candidate h=2,3, B=20, training targets, finite Gaussian scalar outcomes, seeded 7/89 NumPy PCG64 normal/Mammen multipliers, independent-curve row design and valid consecutive candidate domain.

One fixed FPCA basis fitted at maximum candidate h, identical rowwise Mammen/normal wild multipliers shared across candidate h, k-component pseudo-response, h-specific heteroscedastic standard errors, source higher-method root quantiles, interval widths/centers, all fixed-target projections and full B-by-target-by-h studentized root tensor.

Strictly consecutive ascending candidate grid of size at least 2, valid nonzero source rank, all h >= k, matched target geometry, no repeated independent unit identifiers, no nonfinite data, no degenerate nonzero root zero SE; rejects native fixed multiplier replay and base-R seeds when strict source mode.

Twenty canonical FPCAWildBootstrapTruncationScanResult scientific fields with ordered source-shaped provenance and source-canonical candidate h vector; no native-only RNG match flags or source certification boolean in strict source mode.
Sensitivity of fixed-target centered FPCR inference intervals across predeclared candidate truncations under shared random multipliers, not automatic h selection or simultaneous inference.
